title: Object-oriented C# map
intro: This module teaches how C# organizes code with inheritance, interfaces, records, and equality. You get one base class, many interfaces, and records for immutable data shapes. Composition is the default in services; inheritance is for genuine is-a relationships with a small virtual surface.

overviewDiagram.title: C# OOP building blocks
overviewDiagram.source:
flowchart TD
  START[Design a type] --> CHOICE{Relationship?}
  CHOICE -->|has-a| COMPOSE[Composition\ninject interfaces]
  CHOICE -->|is-a| INHERIT[Inheritance\none base class]
  INHERIT --> POLY[Polymorphism\nvirtual / override]
  COMPOSE --> IFACE[Interfaces\nmany per class]
  IFACE --> DIM[Default Interface Methods]
  START --> DATA{Pure data?}
  DATA -->|yes| RECORD[Records\nvalue equality + with]
  DATA -->|no| CLASS[Class\nidentity + behavior]
  RECORD --> EQ[Equality and hashing\nEquals + GetHashCode]

conceptCards.title: Composition versus inheritance
conceptCards.summary: Compose collaborators through interfaces (has-a). Inherit only for genuine is-a with a stable virtual surface. C# allows one base class.

conceptCards.title: Inheritance
conceptCards.summary: One base class. Constructors chain with base(...). abstract blocks new; sealed blocks further derivation.

conceptCards.title: Polymorphism
conceptCards.summary: virtual opens a dispatch slot. override replaces it. new hides — does not dispatch. sealed override closes the slot.
conceptCards.example: Handler h = new LtiHandler(); h.Name // dispatches to LtiHandler

conceptCards.title: Interfaces
conceptCards.summary: CLR contracts. Many per class. DIM evolves contracts. Explicit implementation hides members from the class surface.

conceptCards.title: Records
conceptCards.summary: record class: heap object, value equality. record struct: copy, value equality. with creates a nondestructive copy.
conceptCards.example: var refreshed = token with { ExpiresAt = newTime }

conceptCards.title: Equality and hashing
conceptCards.summary: Equals and GetHashCode are a pair. IEquatable<T> avoids boxing. Never mutate a dictionary key.

conceptCards.title: C# OOP versus JS/TS
conceptCards.summary: C# types survive as CLR metadata. TypeScript types erase. Nominal versus structural typing drives every difference.
conceptCards.example: AuthHint and CacheEntry are not interchangeable in C#
